title: cinnamon-print
description: describe it, an agent places it, your browser renders it — a docker-in-a-folder composition package that turns fragment images, text and shaders into finished pngs and pdfs, reproducibly.

content.heading: cinnamon-print - describe it, an agent places it, your browser renders it
content: **cinnamon-print** is a self-contained composition package: you describe a graphic — canvas, placed images, text, procedural shaders — and it renders the finished artifact as png or pdf. built for flyers, cover art, zines and social cards.

content.heading: the pitch
content: **describe it** in one json file: `project/layout.json` names the canvas, the `fragment*.png` placements, custom text and fonts. it is the single source of truth.
**an agent places it**: in an interactive session (`make repl`), the opencode agent scans your fragments, lints the layout for overlaps and overflow, and proposes placements with you.
**your browser renders it**: the compose script generates the html, applies a pandoc template, and renders through your browser in headless mode — one pipeline, both png and pdf.
**reproducibly**: the whole environment (pandoc, node, your browser, fonts, opencode) is built with nix inside docker — the only prerequisite is docker itself, no unix knowledge required.

content.heading: the frag bench — live shader synthesis
content: the distinctive bit: custom abstract textures and raster elements without heavy GPU dependencies in the container. your running browser (`make serve`) becomes the client-side WebGL worker.

an agent authors GLSL fragment shaders into `resources/shaders/`; the frag bench tab detects new and updated `.frag` files and compiles them live into high-resolution `` swatches. curate the outputs in the browser and drag them straight into `resources/fragments/` as `fragment*.png` assets — from there the standard lint-and-compose pipeline places them in the layout.

shader authoring has its own conventions doc (`resources/shaders/SHADER-NOTES.md`), a font-to-GLSL bitmap rasterizer (`scripts/font-to-glsl.py`), and example shaders that render text — including one set in a real ttf rasterized to bitmaps.

content.heading: current state
content: the compose pipeline is working end to end: layout linting (`make check-layout`), algorithmic re-stacking (`make arrange`), single-shot renders to png and pdf (`make png` / `make pdf`), and a livereload preview server on port 8899.
the frag bench is the active work-in-progress: live shader indexing and the drag-to-compose flow exist; the surface is being sanded as it gets used.
agent-assisted interactive mode runs on opencode with a mounted skill (`imagework-compose`) that drives the scan / lint / place / rebuild loop.

content.heading: github repository
content.content: windows support is a work in progress; the Linux REPL is experimental
